qt: to the Commission Piotr Müller (ECR) Subject:

Although the EU claims to be cutting off Russia’s energy revenues, the 21st sanctions package still leaves the door open for EU shipowners to transport Russian LNG to third countries. This exemption was reportedly kept in place under pressure from Greece, whose companies operate most of the specialist tankers capable of servicing the Yamal terminal. In practice, this means that while the EU intends to ban imports of Russian LNG into its own market from 1 January 2027, it is simultaneously allowing European firms to keep handling those exports and supplying Russia with the funds to wage its war against Ukraine. Such an approach undermines the credibility of EU sanctions policy and puts the interests of a select few shipowners ahead of European security. In light of the above: 1.
How does the Commission justify allowing EU businesses to continue shipping Russian LNG to third countries when the proceeds from its sale are funding Russia’s war budget?

Does the Commission consider it consistent with the objectives of EU sanctions policy to ban the purchase of Russian LNG within the Union while allowing EU businesses to continue enabling Russia to sell it on third-country markets?
Will it propose an outright ban on EU entities providing transport, insurance and technical services linked to Russian LNG exports, and if so, when?
